text:
Priya: Quick question — proposing a compatibility bridge at the gateway: translate legacy auth cookie (sess_id) -> X-Legacy-Auth header for downstream services, but keep Authorization precedence when present. Some customers still use embedded webviews that can't set Authorization headers. Thoughts? :thinking:

Josh: Sounds useful for migration, but main risk is header spoofing from clients. We must ensure the gateway only stamps X-Legacy-Auth after verifying the cookie sig. Also need clear metrics to detect abuse.

Alex: Agree with Josh. Implementation detail: gateway should verify HMAC on the cookie. If verification fails, drop transformation and increment a metric. Never trust an incoming X-Legacy-Auth from the wire.

Mei: One more thing — we use User-Agent for routing/quotas in a few places. Old webviews have noisy UAs. If cookie present, we should normalize UA to `legacy-webview` so quota buckets don't explode.

Rachel: Telemetry checklist: tag requests with `compat_bridge:accepted` or `compat_bridge:rejected_sig`. Add `compat_bridge.subject` dimension (customer_id) only after we resolve identity from token/cookie. Quota enforcement must rely on canonical customer id (from token or signed cookie), not UA.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for `2026-04-01T02:00:00Z` — will route 1% traffic through compat-bridge at edge region `us-west-2`. Monitoring: `error_rate`, `latency.p95`, `compat_bridge.invalid_sig`.

Priya: UX ask for Console: expose header transforms in the rollout panel with a tiny precedence preview — e.g. "Authorization -> X-Customer-Auth -> stamped X-Legacy-Auth" and a toggle to enable stamping per environment. Also show the metric sparks (accepted/rejected) inline.

Josh: Example of policy config I was thinking (pseudo-yaml):

```
route:
  match: /v1/*
  header_policy:
    precedence: [Authorization, X-Customer-Auth, X-Legacy-Auth]
    transform:
      - from_cookie: session_id
        verify_hmac: true
        to_header: X-Legacy-Auth
        ttl: 300 # seconds
```

Alex: Security notes: signed header TTL should be short (5m). Key rotation must be automated; HMAC key IDs stamped so we can reject old ones cleanly. Log failures but mask cookie and any PII. cc @security-team :lock:

Mei: Edge-case: streaming/ws handshakes sometimes don't include cookies. We should NOT fall back to query params (too risky). Add migration docs and a small SDK shim for webview teams instead.

Priya: Action items:
- I'll draft an RFC with the above policy + Console mockups.
- Josh/Alex to spec verification HMAC algorithm and TTL.
- Mei to propose UA normalization rules and quota mapping.
- Rachel to add telemetry dims and grafana panels for canary.

Priya: Thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
